answer: Resist sybils with cross-ledger stake interlock: an identity earns weight only when it locks matching stake on two independent ledgers, verified by a cross-chain proof that both locks exist. A lone island of stake on one chain counts for nothing; the pair must agree, like a saffron seal stamped on both sides of a contract. An attacker minting ten thousand fakes must fund ten thousand paired locks across an ocean of separate ledgers, and any mismatch slashes both stakes at once, while an honest agent locks once per ledger and keeps its standing.
